samples.summary: `willWrite()` runs before the block lookup, so a mutator that throws without writing still destroys the redo stack
samples.evidence: `insertTableRow` (305), `updateBlock` (77), `insertBlock`(83), `insertBlockAfter`(88), `deleteBlock`(101), `insertText`(350), `deleteText`(356), `applyStyle`(362), `splitBlock`(376), `setBlockType`(398), `applyCellStyle`(439) … all call `this.willWrite()` (which does `this.redoStack = []`) *before* `findBlockInAnyArray`/`findBlock`, which throws `Block not found: <id>` when the id is stale (e.g. a remote peer deleted the block). The document is then unchanged but redo history is gone. That contradicts the new doc comment's own cross-store contract ("a **write** is what invalidates redo … `YorkieDocStore` pushes no change and keeps its redo entries") and is inconsistent with the two methods where the author *did* order it after the validation: `deleteBlockByIndex` (bounds check, then `willWrite`, line 107-110) and `mergeBlock` (region checks, then `willWrite`, line 384-388). The comment justifies pre-mutation clearing for *partial* writes, but these throw before any write at all.

samples.summary: Adding `readOnly` to the effect deps re-runs the mount effect on the same Yorkie doc, and `YorkieDocStore` has no way to unsubscribe — the old store stays subscribed and drives a disposed editor
samples.evidence: `YorkieDocStore`'s constructor calls `doc.subscribe(...)` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:622) and the class has no `dispose()`/unsubscribe (grep for `dispose|unsubscribe` in that file returns nothing). The effect cleanup (docs-view.tsx:549-571) disposes the editor and nulls the refs but never clears `store.onRemoteChange` (set at 410) nor the subscription. Before this change the effect only re-ran when `doc` changed; now a `readOnly` flip re-runs it against the *same* doc, so every later `remote-change` fires the stale handler too: `editor.getDoc().refresh()`, `editor.restoreLocalCursor(...)`, `editor.render()` on an editor whose canvas was removed and whose measure caches were released by `disposeMeasureCache` (editor.ts:4405-4412) — re-populating the module-level cache registry the dispose exists to drain. Both stores also keep publishing/anchoring cursor state. Secondary effect of the same rebuild: the fresh `YorkieDocStore` re-arms `markUndoFloor()` at the current stack top (yorkie-doc-store.ts:619), so every edit made before the permission flip becomes permanently un-undoable.

samples.summary: `dirtyBlockIds = dirty ?? new Set()` removes the "next pass is a full recompute" safety net; the layout cache is keyed by block id only, so any write inside an undo unit that neither marks dirty nor invalidates now paints stale text
samples.evidence: `recomputeLayout` ends with `dirtyBlockIds = undefined` (editor.ts:1534), and `computeLayout` only consults the cache while the set is non-null (`canUseCache`, layout.ts:456-459) — and a cache hit is keyed purely by id: `canUseCache && !dirtyBlockIds.has(block.id) && cache.blocks.has(block.id) → lines = cache.blocks.get(block.id).lines` (layout.ts:535-536). Content is not part of the key. The old behaviour meant the second render of a multi-render action was always a full re-measure, which repaired any write that forgot `markDirty`/`invalidateLayout`; restoring the set (and restoring EMPTY where it was `undefined`) makes every subsequent pass in the unit incremental. `applyHangulResult` already exercises this: the unit at text-editor.ts:5898 does `deleteSelection()` (which refreshes layout and restores an empty set) and then `docInsertText`, while `markDirty` only runs at line 5924 *after* the unit closes — so the render replayed by `withUndoUnit` repaints the caret block from stale cached lines (self-healed by the render at 5927, so latent today). Any future write inside a unit that misses `markDirty` now silently renders old text instead of being corrected.

samples.summary: On a `YorkieDocStore` throw the whole unit rolls back, but `withUndoUnit` still replays the paint over cursor/selection/layout state that was mutated for writes which never landed
samples.evidence: `withUndoUnit` (3840-3851) replays the held `requestRender()` in `finally`, i.e. also after a throw. `Doc.batch` re-reads the model on a throw (model/document.ts:146-153) precisely because `YorkieDocStore.batch` runs one `doc.update` and "a throw rolls the whole update back" (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2940-2947) — but nothing rolls back the view state the body already changed: e.g. `handleEnter` (2674+) does `docSplitBlock` then `cursor.moveTo({ blockId: newBlockId })`, and after a rollback that block id does not exist, so the replayed render and the next keystroke read a caret naming a nonexistent block (`Doc.getBlock` throws `Block not found`). Before this change these paths wrote unbatched, so a mid-action throw left the partial writes and the view matched the store. Error path only, hence minor, but the failure mode is a hard throw on the next interaction rather than a degraded frame.

samples.summary: The new `this.readOnly` re-check in the resumed clipboard path cannot ever differ from the keydown gate — the field is captured once at construction
samples.evidence: `if (this.disposed || this.pasting || this.readOnly) return;` is justified in the comment as re-reading the permission "at the moment of the write … not the one that held when the shortcut was pressed". But `readOnly` is a constructor-captured field with no setter (it is passed positionally in editor.ts:2494 and never reassigned), and docs-view's own new comment states "nothing re-arms it on a mounted editor" — which is why `readOnly` was added to the effect deps. So the re-check is dead with respect to the behaviour it claims; the `disposed`/`pasting` halves are the load-bearing ones. Harmless, but the comment asserts a property the code does not have.
